items.title: 6.5.1 Key Features of the Hyperbola (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 200-202: 6.5.1 Key Features (vertices to asymptotes) with Figure 6.23, Note on joint equation, rectangular hyperbola, Second definition and Note

blocks.text: Pichhle hisse mein humne hyperbola ki standard equation \(\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\) nikali. Ab is equation ko 'parhna' seekhte hain: is se curve ke kaun kaun se khaas points aur lines nikalti hain. Yeh bilkul aisa hai jaise kisi shehar ka naqsha dekh kar uske bare chowk, sarkein aur hudood pehchan lena. Har feature ka ek chhota sa wajah wala hisaab hai; formula ratne ke bajaye yeh wajah samajh lein to kabhi nahi bhoolega. Har feature ke saath hum yeh bhi dekhenge ke ellipse mein woh cheez kaisi thi, kyun ke dono ka muqabla karne se farq sab se jaldi samajh aata hai aur exam mein ghalti ka imkaan kam ho jata hai.

items: Vertices (chotiyan): equation mein \(y = 0\) rakhein to \(x = \pm a\). Is liye \(A'(-a, 0)\) aur \(A(a, 0)\) hyperbola ke vertices hain, yani woh points jahan curve apni axis ko kaat-ti hai.
Transverse Axis: dono vertices ko jorne wala line segment \(A'A\) transverse axis (ya focal axis) kehlata hai, kyun ke foci bhi isi line par hain. Is ki lambai \(2a\) hai.

Conjugate Axis: centre se guzarne wali aur transverse axis par perpendicular line conjugate axis kehlati hai. \(x = 0\) rakhein to \(y^2 = -b^2\) aata hai, jo real numbers mein mumkin nahi; yani hyperbola \(y\)-axis ko kabhi nahi kaat-ti. Phir bhi hum \(y\)-axis par do points \(B'(0, -b)\) aur \(B(0, b)\) lete hain; segment \(B'B\) ko conjugate axis kehte hain aur is ki lambai \(2b\) hai.
Foci: foci \((\pm c, 0)\) par hain aur hamesha transverse axis par hote hain. Hyperbola mein \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\), is liye ellipse ke ulat yahan \(a > b\), \(a < b\) ya \(a = b\), teeno mumkin hain.
Centre: dono foci ko jorne wale segment ka midpoint \(C(0, 0)\) hyperbola ka centre hai. Yahi transverse axis ka bhi midpoint hai.

Symmetry: \(x\) ki jagah \(-x\) aur \(y\) ki jagah \(-y\) rakhne se equation nahi badalti, kyun ke dono square mein hain. Is liye hyperbola dono axes aur origin ke lihaaz se symmetric hai, yani aaine ki tarah dono taraf ek jaisi.
Eccentricity: hyperbola ki eccentricity \(e = \frac{c}{a}\) hai. Kyun ke \(c > a\), is liye \(e > 1\). Eccentricity batati hai ke curve kitni 'khuli' hai: \(e\) jitna bara, branches utni chauri.

blocks.text: Ab in features ko ek tasveer ki shakal mein sochiye. Ek seedhi sarak (transverse axis) hai jis par do chirag (foci) lage hain. Sarak ke beech mein ek chowk (centre) hai. Chowk se dono taraf \(a\) faasle par curve sarak ko chhooti hai (vertices), aur chirag us se bhi aage \(c\) faasle par hain. Yani sarak par tarteeb yeh hai: \(F'\), \(A'\), \(C\), \(A\), \(F\). Ellipse mein foci curve ke andar the; hyperbola mein foci har branch ke 'andar' yani mor ke peeche hain, aur centre do branches ke darmiyan khali jagah mein hai. Conjugate axis sarak ko chowk par seedha kaat-ne wali gali hai, jis par curve ka koi point nahi.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ellipse \(y\)-axis ko kaat-ta hai magar hyperbola nahi, kyun? \(x = 0\) rakhne par ellipse mein \(y^2 = b^2\) aata hai (real points \((0, \pm b)\)), jab ke hyperbola mein \(y^2 = -b^2\), jis ka koi real hal nahi. Is liye hyperbola mein \(B(0, b)\) aur \(B'(0, -b)\) curve ke points NAHI hain; yeh sirf conjugate axis batane aur asymptotes banane ke liye nishaan lagaye jate hain.
Aur \(b\) kabhi \(a\) se bara kyun ho sakta hai? Ellipse mein \(a\) hamesha bari semi-axis thi. Hyperbola mein \(a\) bas woh number hai jo POSITIVE term ke neeche ho, chahe chhota ho ya bara. Teeno mein sab se bara hamesha \(c\) hota hai.

items: Directrices: hyperbola \(\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\) ki do directrices hain, jo vertical lines \(x = \pm\frac{a}{e}\) hain.
Latus Rectum: focus se guzarne wali woh chord jo transverse axis par perpendicular ho, latus rectum kehlati hai (jama: latera recta). Har latus rectum ki lambai \(\frac{2b^2}{a}\) hai.

Parametric Equations: har real \(\theta\) ke liye jahan \(\theta \ne (2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2}\) (\(n\) integer), point \((a\sec\theta, b\tan\theta)\) hyperbola \(\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\) par hota hai. Is liye hyperbola ki parametric equations \(x = a\sec\theta\), \(y = b\tan\theta\) hain.

Foci \(y\)-axis par: agar foci \((0, \pm c)\) par hon to \(x\) aur \(y\) ke kirdaar badal jate hain aur standard equation \(\frac{y^2}{a^2} - \frac{x^2}{b^2} = 1\) ban jati hai, vertices \((0, \pm a)\).
\(a\), \(b\) aur \(e\) ka rishta: \(b^2 = c^2 - a^2\) mein \(c = ae\) rakhein to \(b^2 = a^2e^2 - a^2\), yani \(b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1)\). Yeh formula sawalon mein bahut kaam aata hai.

Branches: equation ko \(\frac{x^2}{a^2} = 1 + \frac{y^2}{b^2} \ge 1\) likhein. Is se \(x^2 \ge a^2\), yani \(|x| \ge a\): ya to \(x \ge a\) ya \(x \le -a\). Yani hyperbola do hisson par mushtamil hai jinhein branches kehte hain. \(-a < x < a\) ke darmiyan curve ka koi hissa nahi, kyun ke wahan \(y\) imaginary aata hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh formulas aaye kahan se? Chaliye har ek ko khud check karte hain.
Latus rectum: equation mein \(x = c\) rakhiye: \(y^2 = b^2\left(\frac{c^2}{a^2} - 1\right) = \frac{b^4}{a^2}\), yani \(y = \pm\frac{b^2}{a}\). Chord ke do siron ka faasla \(\frac{2b^2}{a}\) hai.
Parametric form: \(\frac{a^2\sec^2\theta}{a^2} - \frac{b^2\tan^2\theta}{b^2} = \sec^2\theta - \tan^2\theta = 1\), yeh trigonometry ki mashhoor identity hai. \(\theta = (2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2}\) is liye nikale ke wahan \(\sec\theta\) aur \(\tan\theta\) defined hi nahi.
Directrices: \(e > 1\) hai, is liye \(\frac{a}{e} < a\). Yani directrices centre aur vertices ke beech, us khali jagah mein hoti hain jahan curve hai hi nahi.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(\frac{x^2}{25} - \frac{y^2}{144} = 1\) ke liye latus rectum aur directrices kya hongi? Pehle \(a = 5\), \(b = 12\), \(c = \sqrt{25 + 144} = 13\), \(e = \frac{13}{5}\). Latus rectum \(\frac{2 \cdot 144}{5} = \frac{288}{5}\), directrices \(x = \pm\frac{a}{e} = \pm\frac{25}{13}\). Dekhiye \(\frac{25}{13} < 5\): directrices vertices se andar hain, jaisa upar kaha.

Ab asymptotes ki baat. Socho aap ek lambi seedhi sarak ke saath saath chalne wali pagdandi par chal rahe hain. Shuru mein pagdandi sarak se door hai, magar aage ja kar woh sarak ke itna qareeb aa jati hai ke door se dono ek hi lagti hain, phir bhi pagdandi kabhi sarak par nahi charhti. Hyperbola ki branches aur asymptotes ka yahi rishta hai. Graph banate waqt asymptotes pehle khench lein to branches sahi shakal mein khud ban jati hain.

Asymptotes: hyperbola ki ek bahut ahem khoobi, jo ellipse mein nahi hoti, asymptotes hain. Asymptote (woh line jis ke qareeb graph jata hai magar chhoota nahi) ki definition yeh hai: curve \(y = f(x)\) ki asymptote woh line \(y = g(x)\) hai jis ke liye
\[\lim_{x \to \pm\infty}[f(x) - g(x)] = 0\]
yani bohat door ja kar curve aur line ka farq zero ki taraf jata hai.

Hyperbola \(\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\) se \(\frac{y^2}{b^2} = \frac{x^2}{a^2} - 1\), yani \(y^2 = \frac{b^2}{a^2}x^2 - b^2\). Dono taraf \(x^2\) se divide kar ke limit lein:
\[\lim_{x \to \pm\infty} \dfrac{y^2}{x^2}\]
\[= \lim_{x \to \pm\infty}\left(\dfrac{b^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{b^2}{x^2}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{b^2}{a^2}\]

blocks.alt: Pale yellow panel par cyan hyperbola, magenta X aur Y axes, aur do kaali asymptotes y = (b/a)x aur y = -(b/a)x jo O par katti hain. x-axis par vertices A'(-a, 0), A(a, 0) aur foci F'(-c, 0), F(c, 0); branches asymptotes ke qareeb hoti jati hain.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.23: Hyperbola aur us ki asymptotes y = ±(b/a)x (kitab ki figure ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing)

blocks.text: Yani jab \(x \to \pm\infty\), to \(\frac{y^2}{x^2} \to \frac{b^2}{a^2}\), is liye \(\frac{y}{x} \to \pm\frac{b}{a}\). Is ka matlab hai ke bohat door ja kar curve lines \(y = \pm\frac{b}{a}x\) jaisi ho jati hai; yahi do (tirchhi) asymptotes hain, jaisa Figure 6.23 mein dikhaya gaya. Asymptotes curve ko kabhi nahi milti, magar curve ke point ka un se faasla zero ki taraf jata rehta hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kitab ki dalil slope batati hai. Ab dekhte hain ke farq waqai zero ki taraf jata hai. Upar daayen hissa lijiye: \(y = \frac{b}{a}\sqrt{x^2 - a^2}\), \(x > a\). Yahan conjugate (jor) se multiply aur divide karne ki trick lagti hai:
\[y - \dfrac{b}{a}x = \dfrac{b}{a}\left(\sqrt{x^2 - a^2} - x\right)\]
\[= -\dfrac{b}{a} \cdot \dfrac{a^2}{\sqrt{x^2 - a^2} + x}\]
Jab \(x \to \infty\) to denominator bohat bara hota jata hai, is liye farq 0 ki taraf jata hai, magar kabhi bilkul 0 nahi hota (curve line se zara neeche hi rehti hai). Socho aap deewar ki taraf har qadam pichhle qadam ka aadha chalte hain: deewar ke qareeb se qareeb tar hote jate hain magar kabhi chhoote nahi.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text:
Dono asymptotes ki mushtarka (joint) equation yeh hai:
\[\left(y + \dfrac{b}{a}x\right)\left(y - \dfrac{b}{a}x\right) = 0\]
\[y^2 - \dfrac{b^2}{a^2}x^2 = 0\]
\[\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 0\]

Rectangular Hyperbola, ek khaas soorat: agar \(\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\) mein \(a\) aur \(b\) barabar ho jayein to hyperbola \(x^2 - y^2 = a^2\) banti hai, jise rectangular hyperbola kehte hain. Is soorat mein asymptotes ek doosre par perpendicular hoti hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein is paragraph ke baad jumla chhapa hai: "This is obtained by replacing the constant term 1 with 0 in the standard equation." Yeh jumla asal mein upar wale Note ke bare mein hai: asymptotes ki joint equation \(\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 0\) standard equation mein 1 ki jagah 0 rakhne se milti hai. Rectangular hyperbola \(b = a\) lene se banti hai, 1 ko 0 karne se nahi.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Rectangular hyperbola ki asymptotes perpendicular kyun? \(b = a\) ho to asymptotes \(y = x\) aur \(y = -x\) hain; slopes \(1\) aur \(-1\), aur \(1 \times (-1) = -1\). Is ki eccentricity bhi hamesha ek hi hoti hai: \(c^2 = a^2 + a^2 = 2a^2\), is liye \(e = \sqrt{2}\). Yeh MCQs mein aksar poocha jata hai.
Second definition of Hyperbola

Hyperbola ki ek doosri definition bhi hai: agar point \(P\) is tarah chale ke us ka ek fixed point \(F\) (focus) se faasla aur ek fixed line (directrix) se faasla, in dono ka ratio hamesha ek constant \(e\) ho, aur \(e > 1\) ho, to \(P\) ka locus (raasta) eccentricity \(e\) wali hyperbola hai.
Yani agar \(\frac{|PF|}{|PM|} = e\), jahan \(e > 1\) aur \(M\) directrix par \(P\) se perpendicular ka paaon hai, to \(P\) ka locus hyperbola hai.

Is ratio ka matlab samajhiye. \(e > 1\) ka matlab hai ke \(|PF| > |PM|\): curve ka har point focus se, directrix ke muqable mein zyada door hai. Misaal ke taur par \(e = 2\) ho to har point focus se directrix ke muqable mein dugna door hoga. Ellipse mein \(e < 1\) tha, yani points focus ke zyada qareeb the, aur parabola mein \(e = 1\), yani dono faasle barabar. Is tarah eccentricity ek hi number se teeno conics ko alag kar deti hai.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Hyperbola ki equation is definition se bhi nikali ja sakti hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Chaliye woh derivation hum khud karte hain. Focus \(F(ae, 0)\) aur directrix \(x = \frac{a}{e}\) lijiye, \(e > 1\). Point \(P(x, y)\) ke liye \(|PF|^2 = e^2|PM|^2\), aur \(|PM| = \left|x - \frac{a}{e}\right|\). Is liye
\[(x - ae)^2 + y^2 = e^2\left(x - \dfrac{a}{e}\right)^2\]
\[x^2 - 2aex + a^2e^2 + y^2\]
\[= e^2x^2 - 2aex + a^2\]
\[x^2(e^2 - 1) - y^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1)\]
\[\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} - \dfrac{y^2}{a^2(e^2 - 1)} = 1\]
\(b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1)\) rakhein to yeh bilkul \(\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\) hai. Mazedar baat: ek hi focus-directrix usool se \(e < 1\) par ellipse, \(e = 1\) par parabola aur \(e > 1\) par hyperbola banti hai. Yeh teeno ek hi khandaan ke rukn hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Hyperbola \(\frac{x^2}{16} - \frac{y^2}{9} = 1\) ke saare features nikalte hain. Pehle pehchan: \(x^2\) positive hai, to \(a^2 = 16\), \(b^2 = 9\), yani \(a = 4\), \(b = 3\), aur \(c = \sqrt{16 + 9} = 5\).
Vertices \((\pm 4, 0)\); foci \((\pm 5, 0)\); transverse axis 8; conjugate axis 6.
\(e = \frac{5}{4}\); directrices \(x = \pm\frac{a}{e} = \pm\frac{16}{5}\); latus rectum \(\frac{2b^2}{a} = \frac{18}{4} = \frac{9}{2}\).
Asymptotes \(y = \pm\frac{3}{4}x\); parametric form \(x = 4\sec\theta\), \(y = 3\tan\theta\).
Tasdeeq: \(b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1) = 16\left(\frac{25}{16} - 1\right) = 9\). Sahi!

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Ab ek vertical hyperbola: \(\frac{y^2}{9} - \frac{x^2}{16} = 1\). Is baar positive term \(y^2\) wala hai, is liye curve upar neeche khulti hai aur \(a^2 = 9\) (chhota number!), \(b^2 = 16\). To \(a = 3\), \(b = 4\), \(c = 5\).
Vertices \((0, \pm 3)\); foci \((0, \pm 5)\); \(e = \frac{5}{3}\); directrices \(y = \pm\frac{9}{5}\); latus rectum \(\frac{2 \cdot 16}{3} = \frac{32}{3}\).
Asymptotes: 1 ki jagah 0 rakhiye: \(\frac{y^2}{9} = \frac{x^2}{16}\), yani \(y = \pm\frac{3}{4}x\). Dekhiye, yahan slope \(\frac{a}{b}\) hai, \(\frac{b}{a}\) nahi, kyun ke \(x\) aur \(y\) ke kirdaar badal gaye.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Hyperbola \(x^2 - y^2 = 9\) kis qisam ki hyperbola hai? Is ki asymptotes aur eccentricity kya hain? (Jawab: \(a = b = 3\), yani rectangular hyperbola; asymptotes \(y = \pm x\), jo perpendicular hain; \(e = \sqrt{2}\).)

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Asymptotes yaad rakhne ka sab se aasaan tareeqa: standard equation mein 1 ki jagah 0 rakhiye aur \(y\) nikaaliye. \(\frac{x^2}{16} - \frac{y^2}{9} = 0\) se \(y^2 = \frac{9}{16}x^2\), yani \(y = \pm\frac{3}{4}x\). Is tareeqe mein \(\frac{b}{a}\) ya \(\frac{a}{b}\) ki uljhan hi khatam ho jati hai, aur yeh har qisam ki hyperbola (vertical ho ya shifted) par chalta hai.

Ek nazar peeche: is section mein har feature ek hi equation se nikla. \(y = 0\) rakhne se vertices mile, \(x = 0\) rakhne se pata chala ke \(y\)-axis par koi point nahi. \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\) se foci aur eccentricity, \(x = c\) rakhne se latus rectum, aur bohat bare \(x\) par dekhne se asymptotes. Yani aap ko alag alag formulas ratne ki zaroorat nahi; har cheez equation mein koi khaas value rakh kar khud nikal sakti hai. Agle section mein yahi baatein ek table mein ikatthi ki gayi hain, aur phir dekhenge ke jab centre origin se hat kar \((h, k)\) par chala jaye to kya badalta hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\) ke liye: vertices \((\pm a, 0)\), foci \((\pm c, 0)\), \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\).
2. Transverse axis \(2a\), conjugate axis \(2b\); \(a\) chhota bhi ho sakta hai.
3. \(e = \frac{c}{a} > 1\) aur \(b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1)\).
4. Directrices \(x = \pm\frac{a}{e}\); latus rectum \(\frac{2b^2}{a}\); parametric \((a\sec\theta, b\tan\theta)\).
5. Asymptotes \(y = \pm\frac{b}{a}x\); joint equation: 1 ki jagah 0.
6. Rectangular hyperbola: \(a = b\), asymptotes perpendicular, \(e = \sqrt{2}\).
7. Foci \(y\)-axis par: \(\frac{y^2}{a^2} - \frac{x^2}{b^2} = 1\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Ellipse ki aadat mein bare denominator ko \(a^2\) maan lena. Hyperbola mein \(a^2\) hamesha positive term ke neeche hota hai.
2. \(\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\) ki asymptotes \(y = \pm\frac{a}{b}x\) likh dena. Shortcut: 1 ko 0 karo aur \(y\) nikaalo.
3. \(B(0, \pm b)\) ko curve ke points samajh lena; yeh curve par nahi hote.
4. Directrices \(x = \pm ae\) likh dena (yeh to foci hain); sahi \(x = \pm\frac{a}{e}\) hai.
5. Hyperbola ke liye \(e < 1\) le lena; hyperbola mein hamesha \(e > 1\).
